title: Intravenous injection
what: Medicine is given with a syringe directly into a vein, usually in the bend of the elbow. It works quickly.
why: When medicine needs to act fast, or does not work as a pill or a shot into a muscle, as your doctor prescribes.
tell_doctor: If you have felt unwell or fainted during injections before
If your veins are hard to find

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: It is usually better not to come hungry, unless your doctor said otherwise.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A sleeve that is easy to roll up above the elbow.

bring: The medicine, if you bought it yourself
steps: A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
The nurse puts the needle into a vein
The band is removed, and the medicine is given slowly
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on
feel: Sometimes warmth or a taste in the mouth from the medicine. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
You are usually asked to sit for 10 to 15 minutes after the injection
A small bruise can happen and goes away on its own
red_flags: Swelling of the face or lips, trouble breathing, a rash, or sudden weakness: call emergency services
The arm along the vein becomes red, swollen, and painful

faq.q: Why is the medicine given slowly?
faq.a: Many medicines cause unpleasant feelings if given fast. Slowly is safer.
You are usually asked to sit for 10 to 15 minutes. This shows whether you tolerate the medicine well.

reminders.text: IV injection soon. Wear a top with an easy sleeve and eat something, unless your doctor said otherwise.
